name: A Terminal Fiber Forces Lower and Upper Directed Root Cycles
statement: Assume the small two-connected interval is terminal under both one-concept addition to $K$ and one-concept deletion from $A$. Every nonempty passive shore contains a lower active root, and every nonempty complementary shore contains an upper deletion root. Both root sets have at least two members. On the lower roots there is a loopless directed graph of positive out-degree in which $d\to e$ is separated by a shore containing $e$ but not $d$, together with an isolated peripheral blocker cell, a non-root common owner, and an ample shore gate. The graph contains a directed cycle of length at least two; complement duality gives an analogous upper-root cycle.
proof: The passive-shore root theorem gives the lower assertions, and applying it to the complementary ample pair gives the upper assertions and a two-block chain beginning and ending with the respective roots. Each lower root has a peripheral blocker shore that omits it; choose a different lower root in that shore as its outgoing neighbor. The common-owner theorem supplies a shore owner of carrier depth at least two, hence outside the lower-root set. Every root has a nonloop outgoing edge, so finiteness yields a directed cycle and at least two roots. Applying the same argument to the complementary pair gives the upper cycle.
